Make the wolf a proper expressive furry illustrated character, not a robot, rabbit, Yeti, or ordinary four-legged wolf. One werewolf, not a pack. sprite: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: ONE transparent-background game sprite for Frostline, a richly shaded retro pixel-art skiing game. Attached monster atlas is STYLE reference only: match its carefully clustered fur shading, navy outlines, restrained 16-bit palette and small-game readability, not its Yeti anatomy. Create one full-body TWO-LEGGED WEREWOLF, three-quarter view facing slightly right and toward the viewer. Upright lean runner, slate-grey wolf fur, cream muzzle/chest, pointed triangular ears, amber eyes under a strong brow, clear long wolf snout and small fangs, clawed hands, digitigrade hind legs. Torn muted plum/maroon villager vest and short trousers, no hat. Proportions are wolf-human, NOT a gorilla/Yeti, rabbit, armored robot or quadruped. Resting ready-to-run pose: arms hanging slightly bent and visibly separated from torso below shoulders; feet apart and both visible with a clear transparent gap between legs. Stable readable head and chest. Single character only, centered, fills canvas with a narrow transparent margin, no floor, cast shadow, snow, text, panels, duplicates or background. Pixel art logically about32x40 pixels with crisp clustered detail rather than big flat geometric blocks; it will be used at32x40 native pixels, so strong silhouette and clean limb separation are essential. Actual alpha transparency.
